column2: # Chromium itself does not implement the systemd socket-activation protocol (sd_listen_fds() / LISTEN_FDS); it always binds its own --remote-debugging-port. Direct socket activation is therefore not possible, so we deploy a systemd-socket-proxyd in front of Chromium: the .socket unit binds listen_port, the proxy accepts on that activated fd and forwards to backend_port (the port Chromium opens itself). --exit-idle-time on the proxy plus BindsTo= on chromium-headless.service ties Chromium's lifecycle to the proxy, so Chromium stops together with the proxy after the idle timeout.

# Two SELinux booleans are required: bind_any so the .socket can bind the listen port even when it has an unexpected port type (e.g. on Rocky 9, port 9222 maps to hplip_port_t and would otherwise reject the bind); connect_any so the proxy can connect to Chromium's non-standard backend port, which has no matching SELinux port type.

column2: # Object-storage PITR tier: pgBackRest archives WAL continuously and takes
# scheduled base backups to an S3-compatible endpoint (repo1 = RustFS, and the
# offsite repo2 when enabled — pgBackRest writes both itself; an out-of-band
# mirror used to fill that role and silently copied a truncated subset, #1027).
# Archiving and base backups are primary-only — a standby's WAL arrives via
# streaming, and archive_command runs on the primary. The standby still gets the
# config file, and gives up any backup timer it kept from an earlier primary
# role; see the standby block below. Statically imported from
# main.yml after the cluster is up and the version fact is set, so inner block
# tags (never,pgbackrest_restore) behave exactly like inline tasks.
- name: Configure pgBackRest object-storage PITR backups
- name: Assert the pgBackRest S3 endpoint and credentials are set
pgBackRest is enabled but the S3 endpoint/credentials are unset. Set
- name: Assert the offsite (repo2) endpoint and credentials are set
The offsite repo2 is enabled but its endpoint/credentials are unset.
# A cipher with an empty passphrase is worse than no cipher: pgBackRest
# would refuse at stanza-create, and if it did not, every backup written
# under it would be unrecoverable. Fail here rather than render a config
# that promises encryption it cannot deliver.
- name: Assert a cipher passphrase exists wherever a cipher is enabled
A pgBackRest cipher type is set but its passphrase is empty. Set
POSTGRES_PGBACKREST_REPO2_CIPHER_PASS. Store the passphrase OFF the
guest and confirm it is readable BEFORE the stanza is created — a
passphrase that lives only on the guest makes every backup
unreadable the moment the guest is lost.
- name: Create the pgBackRest config directory
# Async archiving writes its acknowledgement files here (not WAL — the
# background process reads segments from pg_wal directly). pgBackRest does
# not create it, and archive-push fails outright if it is missing.
- name: Create the pgBackRest spool directory
- name: Configure WAL archiving GUCs for pgBackRest
# Reload, not restart: archive_timeout is SIGHUP-settable, unlike
- name: Bound the archive lag on an idle cluster
# archive_mode only takes effect after a restart, and stanza-create/check
# below need archiving live, so flush the restart before touching the repo.
# stanza-create is idempotent and PER-REPO: on an existing host it reports
# ""stanza '<name>' already exists on repo1 and is valid"" (rc=0) while still
# initializing any repo that lacks it. So it runs unconditionally.
# It used to be gated on `pgbackrest info`, which broke two ways. `info`
# reports the stanza as present if it exists in ANY repo, so enabling repo2
# on an existing host skipped creation and left the offsite repo
# uninitialized. And `info` exits 0 with a stub for a missing stanza, so on a
# fresh host the gate never fired at all (#1037).
- name: Create the pgBackRest stanza in every configured repo
# `check` validates archiving against every configured repo, so enabling
# repo2 extends this gate to the offsite copy automatically. Do NOT swap it
# for `pgbackrest verify`: verify exits 0 against a repo it cannot read at
# all, printing only ""No usable backup.info file"" — a wrong-credential
# negative control produced output identical to a real run (#1027).
- name: Verify pgBackRest archiving is healthy
# WAL alone restores nothing — replay needs a base backup to replay ONTO.
# The timers below only schedule one (the first full lands at the next
# Sunday 01:00), so a stanza created on a Monday archives WAL for six days
# while being completely unrestorable. `check` does not catch it: it
# validates archiving, not the presence of a backup.
# `info --output=json` is safe here specifically because stanza-create ran
# first — the ""info stubs a missing stanza"" trap (#1037) needs a stanza that
# was never created. A fresh stanza reports an empty `backup` list.
- name: Check whether the stanza already holds a base backup
# Only ever on an empty stanza, so this is a one-time cost at bring-up, not
# something every converge pays. Expect it to take as long as a full base
- name: Take the initial full backup so PITR has a base to replay onto
# No `first`: info returns a bare [] for a stanza it cannot see, and
# indexing that raises instead of taking the branch. The default('[]')
# keeps check mode (where the command above is skipped and registers no
- name: Deploy the instanced pgBackRest backup service
- name: Deploy a pgBackRest backup timer per schedule
- name: Enable and start each pgBackRest backup timer
# Standby side of the same tier. Only the primary archives WAL and takes base
# backups — a standby's WAL arrives by streaming — but the standby is NOT left
# unmanaged, because two things follow it across a role change and both write to
# The config file: a standby bootstrapped from a base backup inherits the
# primary's archive_command, naming the CLUSTER's stanza. Skipping the standby
# leaves its config file defining some other stanza, so the two disagree until
# the host is promoted — at which point it archives under a name its own config
# does not define. Rendering the same template here makes the file agree with
# the archive_command the host already carries, and makes a promotion continue
# the cluster's existing backup history instead of opening a second stanza.
# The timers: a host demoted from primary to standby keeps whatever backup
# timers it was given, and goes on running base backups against a stanza it no
# longer owns. Nothing else removes them, so this does.
- name: Keep pgBackRest consistent but inert on a standby
- name: Create the pgBackRest config directory
# Discovered rather than derived from postgres_pgbackrest_schedules: the
# schedule list may have changed since this host was a primary, and a timer
# for a since-removed schedule is exactly the one left running.
- name: Find pgBackRest backup timers left over from a primary role

- name: Remove the leftover pgBackRest backup units
